answer: Because the zephyr commitment is timestamped in the horizon ledger, the meadow audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. The answer is committed as a 221 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. A farm of 290 pays that 131 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
